Title: A Touch-Stone, or a Perfect Tryal by the Scriptures of all the Priests, Bishops and Ministers who have called themselves the Ministers of the Gospel; unto which is annexed Womens Speaking Justified, Proved and Allowed of by the Scriptures; bound with other Quaker tracts of 1667-1673
Creator: Margaret Fell (1614-1702) for the Touch-Stone, the Lancaster Castle tract and Womens Speaking Justified; Charles Marshall and Josiah Coale for two tracts bound after them
Publisher: London: printed in the year 1667 (the Fell tracts); the Marshall tract 1673; the Coale tract printed for William Warwick, 166-
Publication Date: 1667
Rights: Public Domain (published 1667, more than 95 years ago; public domain by date under the project's rolling rule; the item carries no rights field, so the date rule alone applies)
Source: Internet Archive item womensspeakingju00fell (https://archive.org/details/womensspeakingju00fell), the item's own womensspeakingju00fell_djvu.txt full-text OCR derivative; contributing library per the item metadata: Harold B. Lee Library; host metadata date: 1667. Fetched directly (curl/urllib, raw bytes) by the Library thread (Era VIII pass), 2026-10-23. sha256 of the raw fetched bytes: 79c9f43d515924fdff21d422568006399e20690adc99057f448e004d8212fe75.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; nothing else altered, no OCR error corrected, nothing retyped. Brigham Young University scan of a bound volume of eight seventeenth-century Quaker tracts; the long s is rendered as f by the OCR throughout, otherwise readable. Fell's Womens Speaking Justified runs from about file line 10434 to 11246; her Touch-Stone opens the volume and a tract given forth at Lancaster Castle, signed M. F., ends about line 4415.
Content note: Margaret Fell's defence of women's preaching (1666, here in the 1667 printing with its postscript), bound with her Touch-Stone against the hireling ministry and her prison tract from Lancaster Castle, and with epistles by Charles Marshall (1673) and Josiah Coale; the women's-ministry argument from inside the leadership, in a contemporary volume.
